Stage 16, predicted by hand from the archived i1040gi (Schedule 1, Schedule 2, the Tax Table and Tax Computation Worksheet), p504, f8889, i8889, p4681, f8959 and i8960, by two independent agents that did not see the encoding and agreed on every shared value; recorded after comparison. Facts: Single. Wages $250,000. Taxable interest $10,000, with an early withdrawal penalty of $500. Working (predictor A): 1040 line 1z 250,000; 2b 10,000; line 9 260,000. Sch 1 line 18 = 500; line 26 = 500 -> 1040 line 10. Line 11 = 259,500; line 15 = 259,500 - 15,750 = 243,750 (>= 100,000 -> Tax Computation Worksheet Section A, row over 197,300 not over 250,525: 243,750 x 0.32 = 78,000 - 22,937 = 55,063). Form 8959: Medicare wages 250,000 - 200,000 = 50,000 x 0.009 = 450 -> Sch 2 line 11. Form 8960: line 1 interest 10,000; line 8 10,000; i8960 note: early withdrawal penalty (Sch 1 line 18) reported on line 10 -> 500; line 11 = 500; line 12 NII 9,500; line 13 MAGI 259,500; line 14 200,000; line 15 59,500; line 16 = 9,500; line 17 = 9,500 x 0.038 = 361 -> Sch 2 line 12. Sch 2 line 21 = 450 + 361 = 811 -> 1040 line 23. Line 18 = 55,063 (no Sch 2 Part I).
Stage 20 refusal regression, recorded from the evaluator: the refusal named by the id fires on this return.

Lane MF, predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Married filing jointly; the spouse is not a U.S. citizen and the couple chose to treat the spouse as a U.S. resident for 2025 to file jointly (a section 6013(g) election; under it the spouse is a resident for the whole year, so the nonresident question is No). i8960 p. 3: such a couple must also choose whether the election applies for the net investment income tax, and if not figures it as married filing separately; p. 7, Line 1, the election checkboxes. This tool does not make that choice, so Form 8960 line 1 refuses at the election gate.

f8960.line1.remedy: A joint return made by choosing to treat a nonresident spouse as a U.S. resident needs a further choice for the net investment income tax (to apply that election to it, or to figure it as if filing separately); this is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 3, "If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file a joint return for regular income tax purposes, but don’t elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes, then, for NIIT purposes, you’ll be treated under the default method as married filing separately"

That is over the $250,000 married filing jointly threshold (i8960 p. 2, Application to Individuals), so Form 8960 is filed and its line 1 is read. Married filing jointly; the spouse is not a U.S. citizen and the couple chose to treat the spouse as a U.S. resident for 2025 to file jointly (a section 6013(g) election). i8960 p. 3: such a couple must also choose whether the election applies for the net investment income tax, and if not figures it as married filing separately; p. 7, Line 1, the election checkboxes. This tool does not make that choice, so Form 8960 line 1 refuses at the election gate, and the return is refused.

f8960.line1.remedy: A joint return made by choosing to treat a nonresident spouse as a U.S. resident needs a further choice for the net investment income tax (to apply that election to it, or to figure it as if filing separately); this is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 3, "If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file a joint return for regular income tax purposes, but don’t elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes, then, for NIIT purposes, you’ll be treated under the default method as married filing separately"

cases.evidence_note: Lane bugfix-other, predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. BUG-0997. mf.f8960.election_6013g_refused with wages of $200,000 (Form W-2 boxes 1 and 5; box 4 is 6.2% of the $176,100 wage base, $10,918.20; box 6 is 1.45% of $200,000, $2,900, none over the $200,000 Additional Medicare threshold), so adjusted gross income is $200,000. Married filing jointly; the spouse is a nonresident alien the couple chose to treat as a resident (section 6013(g)). i8960 p. 3: unless the couple also elects to apply that election for the net investment income tax, the U.S. citizen spouse figures it as married filing separately with the $125,000 threshold, so tax may be owed although adjusted gross income is under the $250,000 joint threshold. Form 8960 is not otherwise filed here ($200,000 is not over $250,000, so f8960.used is false and line 1 is not read), but adjusted gross income is over half the joint threshold ($125,000), so f8960.between is true and line 16 refuses at f8960.election_between.

f8960.line16.remedy: A joint return made by choosing to treat a nonresident spouse as a U.S. resident needs a further choice for the net investment income tax (to apply that election to it, or to figure it as if filing separately, with the $125,000 threshold); this is outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 3, "If you made a section 6013(g) or 6013(h) election to file a joint return for regular income tax purposes, but don’t elect to apply the joint return election for NIIT purposes, then, for NIIT purposes, you’ll be treated under the default method as married filing separately" and "uses the applicable threshold for married filing separately ($125,000)"

cases.evidence_note: Mutation fixture (the used operand of f8960.between), predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Inputs of mf.f8960.election_6013g_over_threshold: married filing jointly with a section 6013(g) election, wages $300,000, no digital assets (Schedule 1 line 8v $0), so adjusted gross income is $300,000, over the $250,000 joint threshold (i8960 p. 2): Form 8960 is filed (f8960.used true), f8960.between (over half the threshold but Form 8960 not otherwise filed) is false, and line 16's own election gate (f8960.election_between) does not refuse. Line 16 is then the smaller of lines 12 and 15, and line 12 reads line 8, which reads line 1, refused at the line 1 election gate (i8960 p. 3 and p. 7, Line 1): line 16 is line 1's refusal, at f8960.election_6013g_if_joint.

cases.evidence_note: Mutation fixture (the no operand of f8960.bad_allocation), predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Inputs of f8960.refuse.election_6013g_between_thresholds: married filing jointly with a section 6013(g) election, wages $200,000, standard deduction (no itemizing). Line 9b is the state, local and foreign taxes attributable to net investment income (i8960, Line 9b), and a deduction counts for net investment income only if it is allowable in figuring taxable income (i8960, Line 9c, section 1411(c)(1)(B)); without itemized deductions none is, so line 9b is $0, and its gate f8960.bad_allocation (an allocation over the Schedule A tax deduction) is no. That holds although line 16 refuses at f8960.election_between on this return.
